title: NZ 2-4: Dynamic Range, Color Grading, and Sky-Rainbow Techniques in Queenstown Canyon Photography

locations.name: Queenstown, New Zealand
locations.basis: Explicit mention in transcript: "Queenstown. So we got about 30 more minutes here"

summary: The video is a detailed post-processing workflow for landscape imagery captured in New Zealand, focusing on canyon and waterfall scenes. The presenter walks through zone-based edits, RAW adjustments, and multiple creative techniques to control dynamic range, color, and light. Key demonstrations include expanding dynamic range in camera raw, painting light onto rocks and waterfalls, sky recoloring with highlight burn, Orton-style diffusion, cloning out distractions, perspective corrections with warp tools (rule of trapezoids and puppet warp), focus stacking considerations, and culminating in color grading and God-beam effects for dramatic canyon scenes. The speaker also discusses composition choices, cropping, and foreground weight to guide the viewer’s eye toward waterfalls, ferns, and rainbow features, with emphasis on practical, repeatable steps rather than abstract theory.

sections.title: Overview, zone-based composition, and initial planning
concepts: crop strategy to emphasize waterfall and fern
sections.description: Introductory planning session describing zone-based composition, cropping choices to highlight the waterfall-fern relationship, and the rationale for keeping certain elements out of frame.

featured_techniques.technique: Dynamic range expansion in Camera Raw
Edge-focused painting with a large brush to create smooth fade
Sky recoloring via highlight burn (40% opacity) and color switching
Orton effect / diffusion-based softening on foreground
Cloning out distractions / removing people with clone stamp
Perspective warp and the rule of trapezoids to straighten elements
Puppet Warp for precise retiming of flowers / rainbow elements
Auto HDR and Whites adjustments to intensify rainbow areas
God beams / directional side lighting corrections
Selective color adjustments and color grading for cohesive palette
Bracketing mode discussion for exposure planning
